encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry or psychology follow-up for ongoing depression management
allowed_distractors: history of alcohol use, now abstinent for 2 years
mild insomnia, secondary to depression and not separately diagnosed
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: this is a RECURRENT episode — the note must reference prior episode history or prior treatment
CRITICAL: severity is MODERATE — hopelessness, anhedonia, and cognitive symptoms are appropriate but do not describe suicidal ideation with intent or plan (that suggests severe)
do not imply full remission — the patient has current depressive symptoms
do not imply psychotic features such as hallucinations or delusions

active_conditions: major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe without psychotic features
encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry follow-up for severe depression and co-occurring anxiety management
allowed_distractors: one prior psychiatric hospitalization for depression, years ago
remote history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: MDD severity is SEVERE WITHOUT PSYCHOTIC FEATURES — suicidal ideation may be present but hallucinations or delusions must NOT appear in the note
CRITICAL: both MDD and GAD must be independently evidenced — GAD needs excessive uncontrollable worry and somatic symptoms beyond just depressive anxiety
do not describe manic or hypomanic episodes — this is unipolar depression, not bipolar disorder

encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry follow-up for mood stabilization and anxiety management
allowed_distractors: history of cannabis use, currently abstinent
mild insomnia related to the mood disorder
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: Bipolar II means HYPOMANIC episodes, not full manic episodes — do not describe a full manic episode with psychosis or hospitalization for mania, which would indicate Bipolar I
the note must reference prior hypomanic episode history or mood cycling context
GAD must be independently evidenced beyond general mood-related anxiety
do not imply Bipolar I or schizoaffective disorder

encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry or trauma-focused therapy follow-up for PTSD and co-occurring depression
allowed_distractors: history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission for 18 months
mild sleep disturbance overlapping with both conditions
trap_patterns: PTSD must be evidenced by at least one symptom cluster: re-experiencing (flashbacks, intrusive memories, nightmares), avoidance behavior, negative cognitions or mood, or hyperarousal (startle response, hypervigilance)
trauma exposure must be referenced without being gratuitously explicit
MDD must have independent depressive symptom support beyond PTSD mood symptoms
do not imply acute suicidal crisis unless the encounter context specifically warrants it

encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry or primary care behavioral health follow-up for anxiety and panic management
allowed_distractors: history of one mild depressive episode, fully resolved
mild somatic complaints such as headaches and GI upset, attributable to anxiety
trap_patterns: GAD and panic disorder must be INDEPENDENTLY evidenced — they share some symptoms but have different cores: GAD requires chronic excessive uncontrollable worry; panic disorder requires discrete panic attack episodes with physical symptoms and anticipatory anxiety between attacks
CRITICAL: this is panic disorder WITHOUT AGORAPHOBIA — do not describe avoidance of places or situations where escape would be difficult
do not imply major depressive disorder as an active condition

encounter_context: outpatient community mental health center or dual diagnosis program follow-up
allowed_distractors: active tobacco use, ongoing
mild hypertension noted on exam, not the primary concern today
trap_patterns: schizophrenia paranoid type requires paranoid delusions or prominent paranoid ideation — this distinguishes it from other schizophrenia subtypes
both schizophrenia and alcohol use disorder must be independently addressed in assessment and plan
alcohol use disorder MODERATE means approximately 4 to 5 DSM criteria met — not mild and not severe alcohol dependence requiring inpatient detox
do not imply major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder as the primary mood diagnosis — the primary psychotic disorder is schizophrenia

active_conditions: major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry or primary care behavioral health initial or early follow-up for new-onset depression
allowed_distractors: recent identifiable life stressor as precipitating context (bereavement, job loss)
mild anxiety symptoms not meeting full criteria for a separate anxiety disorder
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: this is a SINGLE EPISODE — the note must NOT reference prior depressive episodes; this is the patient's first depressive episode
severity is MODERATE — symptoms are present and functionally impairing but not at the level requiring hospitalization
do not imply suicidal ideation with an active plan (that would suggest severe)
do not describe recurrent or chronic depression — this is a first episode

encounter_context: outpatient psychiatry or behavioral health follow-up for adult ADHD and co-occurring anxiety management
allowed_distractors: history of academic difficulties in childhood, now retrospectively understood as ADHD
mild sleep onset insomnia overlapping with both conditions
trap_patterns: ADHD combined type requires BOTH inattentive AND hyperactive-impulsive symptom clusters to be evidenced — not just one cluster
GAD must be independently supported beyond ADHD-related cognitive difficulties: excessive worry, difficulty controlling worry, and somatic anxiety symptoms should be present
do not imply stimulant misuse or diversion concerns
do not describe psychotic symptoms or primary mood disorder as the chief complaint

active_conditions: adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
encounter_context: outpatient primary care or counseling follow-up after a recent identifiable stressor within the past 3 months
allowed_distractors: mild insomnia related to the adjustment reaction, not separately diagnosed
remote history of one treated depressive episode, fully resolved years ago
trap_patterns: the identifiable stressor must be mentioned in the note (examples: job loss, divorce, medical diagnosis, significant financial stress, relocation)
symptoms must be either disproportionate to the stressor or causing significant functional impairment in work, school, or relationships
do not imply a full major depressive disorder episode — adjustment disorder symptoms are stressor-linked and expected to resolve as the stressor resolves or adaptation occurs
do not imply panic disorder or generalized anxiety disorder as a separate primary diagnosis

encounter_context: outpatient dual diagnosis or addictions psychiatry follow-up for co-occurring substance use, depression, and sleep disorder
allowed_distractors: active tobacco use, ongoing
mild anxiety symptoms secondary to the primary conditions
trap_patterns: all three active conditions must be independently addressed in assessment and plan
alcohol use disorder moderate means approximately 4 to 5 DSM criteria — describe drinking patterns consistent with this severity, not severe physiologic dependence requiring inpatient detox
MDD recurrent moderate requires reference to prior episode history
insomnia disorder must be addressed as a distinct clinical problem with sleep pattern details, not just a symptom mention in passing
